articles.title: Commander Shepard Voice Actors Call for Action to Save Mass Effect
articles.summary: News of BioWare shutting down and the development of Mass Effect Universe ending hit fans hard this week. The community is coming together on a large scale in an attempt to save the beloved sci-fi action role-playing game's future.
body: The Electronic Arts buyout by Saudi Arabia's PIF and private equity made fans uneasy regarding the future of several franchises. And rightfully so, as only a few months in, development studio BioWare was shut down, and its most anticipated project, a new Mass Effect game, was canceled.

The Mass Effect trilogy consists of three revolutionary, narrative-heavy, sci-fi games. It has unique characters with whom players can form strong connections and rich lore that makes for a complex yet engrossing story. Even though Mass Effect 5 (now known as Mass Effect: Universe ) was announced nearly six years ago, it's no surprise that fans were still very much looking forward to it and were heartbroken to discover that the project would not be moving forward. The fanbase is currently doing what it can to save Mass Effect. The scale of the movement is bigger than anyone could've expected — even the Canadian government is considering coming to BioWare's aid.

A fan petition is gaining traction on social media, accumulating 130,000 signatures within three days. Jennifer Hale, Commander Shepard's voice actress, has spoken up on X about the matter, asking fans to help "bring Mass Effect back to life."
points: News of BioWare shutting down and the development of Mass Effect Universe ending hit fans hard this week.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Teaser Reveals Who Was Edited Out of the First Trailer, Fans Say
articles.summary: Marvel fans say the new Avengers: Doomsday teaser might have revealed who was edited out of its first trailer.
body: Marvel Studios didn't not reveal more from its December team-up movie when the Doomsday baseball teaser premiered during Game 1 of the 2026 World Series last night. Focusing more on letting Pedro Pascal's Reed Richards throw Joseph Quinn's Johnny Storm a stretchy pitch as MLB players did their best to fit in, the minute-long TV spot felt more like a cute crossover than an opportunity for new footage – but that doesn't mean fans aren't still all over it.

In between the shots of the Fantastic Four's Earth-828 are, occasionally, what amounts to a few precious seconds of new footage from Avengers: Doomsday. With less than two months left to go until the premiere, Marvel really only took the time to highlight some funny interactions between Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) and characters like Ant-Man (Paul Rudd) and Thor (Chris Hemsworth).

It's…not much. While you might think Steve taking a jab at Thor while wielding Mjolnir is the standout moment, some eagle-eyed fans think it's the scene the former Captain America shares with Ant-Man that we should be paying attention to.

articles.title: Hulu Officially Bringing Back 2000s Fan-Favorite Crime Drama
articles.summary: One of Fox’s most popular TV shows of all time is coming back under Disney. Hulu revealed a first look at Prison Break: Black Creek, a spinoff series set in the same universe as the original.
body: While the teaser doesn’t give a lot to go on, Deadline provides the following description: “A soldier-turned-corrections officer takes a job at one of the deadliest prisons in America to prove just how far she’ll go for someone she loves.” The show will take place at the fictional Black Creek Penitentiary.

Elgin James ( Mayans M.C., The Outlaws ) is Black Creek ​​​​​​'s showrunner. The teaser video reveals that he will also direct, with Vanessa Joy Smith handling cinematography. Dawn Olmstead, who executive produced the original series, returns to that role, while Disney-owned 20th Television is handling production.

As for the cast, Black Creek stars Drake Rodger ( The Winchesters ) as Tommy, Clayton Cardenas ( Mayans M.C.) as Michael “Ghost,” JR Bourne ( Teen Wolf ) as Junior, Georgie Flores ( Famous in Love ) as Andrea, and Myles Bullock ( BMF ) as Darius “Red.” Noah Emmerich ( Murdaugh: Death in the Family, Dark Winds ) will play Callum Faulls, a West Virginia power broker.
points: One of Fox’s most popular TV shows of all time is coming back under Disney.
Hulu revealed a first look at Prison Break: Black Creek, a spinoff series set in the same universe as the original.
The show will take place at the fictional Black Creek Penitentiary.

articles.title: The 20 Most-Played Steam Next Fest Demos Features Troublemaking Students, Farting Hippos
articles.summary: Steam Next Fest is currently in full swing, and developers big and small have released new demos so players can discover their upcoming games. While the event runs through Oct. 26, Valve has already revealed to Polygon what the 20 most popular demos out of the 8,000+ games featured are.
body: Developed and published by Funcore Games, Worst Class Ever is a new asymmetrical friendslop game where a team of trouble-making students tries to mess around with the classroom and each other behind the back of the teacher, who is controlled by another player. Over 300,000 people have played this demo, according to Funcore Games, and it's expected to be released sometime during Q4 2026.

If you've just watched Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 and are in the mood for more, then this shopkeeping sim from Questing Goose Studio and tinyBuild will probably be of interest to you. The game mixes typical shopkeeping gameplay with elements of games like Papers, Please, as the player has to determine whether or not to do business with the people who show up at their counter. If you like what you play of this one, Probably Stolen launches on Oct. 28.

For the fantasy fans out there, ArcheAge Chronicles is an MMORPG from XL Games. While it features all the trappings you'd expect from a game of its ilk, ArcheAge Chronicles features fluid combat closer to Phantom Blade Zero than World of Warcraft. A date for its Steam Early Access launch has not been announced yet.

articles.title: FBI investigating theft of more than 6000 PSA-graded trading cards, including almost 3000 Pokémon cards
articles.summary: The FBI and Santa Ana police are investigating the theft of 6451 PSA-graded cards, including nearly 3000 Pokémon cards, from a FedEx truck in California.
body: PSA confirmed the investigation, saying the orders were stolen on 13th October from a FedEx truck after pickup at its Santa Ana facility.
The company says that "recovering every stolen item and returning it to its owner is our top priority", and that it has given investigators video footage, shipment manifests, and item-level records.

In total, 6451 items were taken. PSA has published a list of every stolen card, including its certification number and, for serialised cards, the serial number. It deactivated the certification numbers and shared the list with marketplace sellers, auction houses, and digital commerce platforms, so the cards can't be easily resold.

According to TheGamer, which broke down the list by category, Pokémon cards account for 2978 of the stolen items, followed by 898 One Piece cards, 880 basketball cards, 640 baseball cards, and 433 football cards. The New York Times reports that the haul is collectively worth more than $963,000.

articles.title: Mass Effect Universe "looked incredible" says creator who claims he advised BioWare
articles.summary: A content creator who claims to have served on a BioWare community council has shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.
body: In a lengthy Twitter/X post (thanks, PC Gamer ), YouTuber Dantics claimed the cancelled game was set more than 600 years after the Reaper War.
He said he'd had access via his role on the "Mass Effect Council" and had seen firsthand what BioWare was developing, and provided feedback during development.

According to Dantics, the game would have centred on a "galactic Cold War" between three major factions, rather than another Reaper-style invasion. Humanity, the Krogan, the Batarians, and others would have allied, with the Council races forming their own alliance and the Geth emerging as a third superpower.
He also mentioned Geth-built megastructures, connections between the Milky Way and Andromeda, and a "shadowy adversary".
points: A content creator who claims to have served on a BioWare community council has shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.

body: The latter game's titular mouse detective has been squished into a cube-like shape and sent to navigate a hellish labyrinth full of sawblades for the rest of his miserable existence. Oh, and the screen goes all black-and-white when you play as him, just like the FPS he comes from.

This might all seem downstream of cynical money devourers like Fortnite, but at least these games share something in both being indie(ish) cartoony pastiches with a gore-slick twist. Besides, Meat Boy is an OG when it comes to invasions of strangers' videogames.

You could play as him in the Bit.Trip games, and in turn CommanderVideo cameoed in Super Meat Boy. If you're too Gen A to understand a single word I just said about the halcyon days of 2010s indie gaming, that's okay. I'll just go lay down and die.

articles.title: Stalker 2's next update has already leaked
articles.summary: PlayStation Asia has reportedly leaked details of an unannounced update coming to Stalker 2: Heart of Chornobyl, 2.1, next week.
body: As shared on the Stalker subreddit, a graphic listing the update's highlights, called The Zone Lookout, was posted to PlayStation Asia's Twitter/X account.
The post said update 2.1 was "out now", but it appears to have gone up early, with the update reportedly due next week. At the time of writing, the tweet is still live.

The image suggests we'll see an increase in A-Life NPC visualisation range, related adjustments to combat and ballistics, fast travel with squad leaders, and other bug fixes and improvements. Beyond that, though, it was otherwise light on detail.
Update 2.0 arrived on 20th August alongside the Cost of Hope expansion, adding binoculars, a fog mechanic, A-Life changes, and "dozens of hours of content".

articles.title: Japan Actors Union pushes for heavy restrictions on AI copying dead actors
articles.summary: The Japan Actors Union, an org consisting of around 2,600 actors and voice actors, recently announced a series of measures to protect the rights of performers in the industry with regard to generative AI (reported in English via Automaton Media ).
body: It's been a hot topic both in Japan and here in the west, with Leon Kennedy actor Nick Apostolides arguing AI voice acting was something of an oxymoron: "AI can speak lines, but there's nothing human behind it," he said.

"It protects the dignity, honor, and legacy of deceased performers from commercial exploitation," said the union (auto-translated from Japanese). "We respect the wishes of the person during their lifetime to the greatest extent, and when generating AI, strict permission from the family (or administrator) who inherits the rights is mandatory to prevent desecration of the deceased."

Given the AI-related catastrophes we've seen in this field of the voicework world, like a facsimile of James Earl Jones slinging AI-generated slurs in Fortnite, these guidelines seem fairly gentle and reasonable. Time will tell if these pushes for actors' rights will take hold on a larger scale within the Japanese entertainment industry and otherwise.

articles.title: 'I drank from the chalice of blood': indie dev scrubs his game of AI-generated voice lines, having previously described the technology as 'anti-human and anti-art'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Well, here's a headscratcher. Paolo Pedercini, developer of Future? No Thanks! recently admitted to using generative AI in his ecosocialist satire while also referring to the technology as "a technofascist, anti-human and anti-art project." Now, the developer has removed several AI generated voice lines from the game, following a backlash to his use of the very technology which the game lampoons.

You might remember Future? No Thanks! from another recent controversy, whereupon the game was briefly delayed after Steam held up its release while it reviewed some fleeting nudity in the game. Pedercini—who also goes by Mollieindustria—received considerable support during that debacle. But the reaction to Future? No Thanks' AI use has been rather less supportive, prompting Pedercini to rework the game and respond to the backlash.

articles.title: Penguin Colony review: A daringly weird horror game whose atmosphere and surprises overcome its rough edges
articles.summary: Something ancient and horrible stirs in the farthest south: Are you bad enough penguin to… not really do much about it?
body: Penguin Colony is a work of cosmic horror that I would recommend to anyone with even a passing interest in scares from the beyond, even though its unique penguin platforming can be frustrating to wrangle. It's a radical recontextualization of an H.P. Lovecraft classic with a clear affection for the writer's storytelling, but also scathing contempt for his racism.

For my money, it's not October without a weird-ass new indie horror game leaving a lasting impression on me, and Penguin Colony has satisfied my annual craving. You are a penguin witnessing the events of the Lovecraft story, At the Mountains of Madness. Your powers are honk, slide, swim, and hop.

Rather than being limited to a specific bird, you are able to possess any penguin you come across, theoretically using different species' abilities to tackle different movement challenges. Aside from using little baby penguins to squeeze into tight spaces, I was almost exclusively a Rockhopper main: Their impressive vertical jump was a boon in many areas. They shoulda hooped instead of investigating The Strange.
